question.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3x+y+7z=5 \\ x-4y+8z=1 \\ -6y+9z=2\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 7 \\ 1 & -4 & b \\ 0 & a & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}c \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b,$ and $c?$

current_example.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}6x+4y=1 \\ x-8y-z=-2 \\ 3x+2y-2z=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/76fbe25754bbca564d39872ef9817754c49a8af7b14c55663d87e416e17e5ac0.svg)

What are the values of $a,$ $b$ and $c?$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}6x+4y+0z=1 \\ x-8y-z=-2 \\ 3x+2y-2z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/9867975d7c037dfc9f9dc3f3a97a54d4616968fa065dab2eb7df63092f9fc42e.svg)

is the coefficient matrix,

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/3f8d3bbb7bd1bba7c64651844edfbd41049ffc8ce5465b1146352cf8d304b13f.svg)

is the column vector of constants, and

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/711c76f79af405029bb73a1120d8bdf588efcc2085f4262af0153e7cc648b105.svg)

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/498541b430e0f3a2f31ae928c91775b7c0264de34e46f3348785e9afbc893b30.svg)

Therefore, $a=6,$ $b=2,$ and $c=-2.$
